security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI unconditionally writes csr_write(CSR_MIP, 0) during sbi_hart_init() (lib/sbi/sbi_hart.c:732) to clear all pending interrupts before S-mode handoff, but the spec explicitly permits any MIP bit to be read-only. If a platform implements a read-only MIP bit that is externally driven (e.g., MEIP from a platform-level interrupt controller), writing 0 has no effect and the pending interrupt remains set. After OpenSBI delegates interrupts to S-mode via mideleg, that stale pending bit fires a spurious interrupt into S-mode before S-mode software is prepared to handle it. Similarly, HSM non-retentive suspend restore at sbi_hsm.c:445 uses csr_set(CSR_MIP, ...) which silently fails on read-only SSIP/STIP bits if the platform chooses to make those read-only.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csr_write(CSR_MIP, <zero or mask>) without subsequent csr_read(CSR_MIP) WARL validation to confirm writable bits were actually cleared; also csr_set(CSR_MIP, <bits>) assuming SSIP/STIP writability without platform capability probe
security_spec.summary: OpenSBI assumes all MIP bits are writable and clears them unconditionally during hart init; spec PR #2974 explicitly permits read-only MIP bits, so platform-tied interrupts may survive the write and cause spurious S-mode traps
